findings.issue_text: [High/bug] EventManager.ts:117 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` accessed without null check; throws TypeError when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/empty (previously guarded by `?.`), breaking bookings without a destination calendar

[High/bug] CalendarService.ts (office365):72 — `createEvent` ignores `credentialId` and always uses `destinationCalendar[0]`; with the per-credential loop, a second O365 member's credential creates the event into the first member's calendar

[High/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):315-317 — In `deleteEvent`, falsy `externalCalendarId` causes comparison against null/undefined id, never matches, and yields `calendarId: undefined`, producing a malformed request (`/calendars/undefined/events`); old code fell back to destination calendar's externalId

[Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):255-258 — In `updateEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy and no destination matches, `calendarId` becomes `undefined` (old "primary"/destination fallback removed), so updates can fail

[Medium/data] handleNewBooking.ts:1098-1100 — Team member destination calendars only collected for `isTeamEventType && schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`, so dynamic collective links never gather members' calendars despite the PR's goal

[Medium/bug] handleNewBooking.ts:1098 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `destinationCalendar` is null, dropping team members' destination calendars instead of initializing the array

[Medium/bug] BaseCalendarService (CalendarManager.ts / CalendarService.ts) — `createEvent`/`listCalendars` also only use `destinationCalendar[0]` and ignore `credentialId`; per-credential loop will create events into the wrong calendar for non-Google providers

[Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):145-149 — When credential's destination calendar isn't found, `createEvent` silently falls back to `"primary"`, booking the event on the wrong calendar instead of erroring

[Medium/bug] EventManager.ts:~500-530 — In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, if the credential filter finds nothing and DB fetch fails or app slug is missing, `credential` remains `undefined` and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` throws a TypeError on a previously non-null path

[Medium/performance] EventManager.ts & handleCancelBooking.ts — `prisma.credential.findUnique` runs sequentially inside a per-reference/destination loop with duplicated logic; N destinations cause N sequential round-trips that could be batched

[Low/test_gap] webhook.e2e.ts:249 — No test covers the new multi-destination collective flow (multiple destinationCalendar entries / multiple calendar references on update and delete), the core behavior change of the PR
[Low/bug] CalendarManager.ts:229 — Typo fix changing "organiser" to "organizer" is a behavioral string change not covered by i18n TODO; tests/snapshots asserting the old string will break

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] EventManager.ts:117 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` accessed without null check; throws TypeError when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/empty (previously guarded by `?.`), breaking bookings without a destination calendar
matched_golden_ids: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` becomes undefined (via destructuring/selection), and later accessing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` causes a TypeError due to missing null/undefined checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] CalendarService.ts (office365):72 — `createEvent` ignores `credentialId` and always uses `destinationCalendar[0]`; with the per-credential loop, a second O365 member's credential creates the event into the first member's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now derives the calendar to write to via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses only `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` to build the URL. Meanwhile, the core flow was changed to create events per destination/credential: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops destinations and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, and `CalendarManager.createEvent` calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. Office365’s implementation neither accepts nor uses the passed `credentialId` (signature still `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in the diff) and has no logic to select the destination calendar matching the current credential, so when multiple O365 destination calendars exist the per-credential loop can create events into the first destination calendar instead of the intended one (and the signature mismatch is itself a compile-time defect against the updated `Calendar` interface).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):315-317 — In `deleteEvent`, falsy `externalCalendarId` causes comparison against null/undefined id, never matches, and yields `calendarId: undefined`, producing a malformed request (`/calendars/undefined/events`); old code fell back to destination calendar's externalId

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the fallback logic in `deleteEvent` (and similarly in `updateEvent`) was changed from using the destination calendar’s `externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the exact case described), the `find` compares against `undefined` and will almost always return no match, yielding `undefined` instead of the destination calendar’s externalId. This is a real behavior regression compared to the old code’s fallback and can result in an undefined/incorrect calendarId being used for the delete request (or falling back to `primary` elsewhere, deleting from the wrong calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):255-258 — In `updateEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy and no destination matches, `calendarId` becomes `undefined` (old "primary"/destination fallback removed), so updates can fail

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. If `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/""), the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (falsy), which will typically yield no match and thus `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains calendars. Unlike `createEvent`, there is no `|| "primary"` fallback shown for update, so this can cause updates to call the Google API with an undefined `calendarId` and fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] handleNewBooking.ts:1098-1100 — Team member destination calendars only collected for `isTeamEventType && schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`, so dynamic collective links never gather members' calendars despite the PR's goal

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking, `teamDestinationCalendars` is only populated inside `teamMemberPromises` when `isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` (and later only pushed to `evt.destinationCalendar` under the same condition). The diff does not include any other path that aggregates destination calendars for multi-user/dynamic scenarios outside COLLECTIVE, so if the intended behavior was to include all participating users’ destination calendars in those cases, this change is incomplete. The claim about the PR’s goal can’t be verified from the diff alone, so this is best treated as a scope/edge-case concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] handleNewBooking.ts:1098 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `destinationCalendar` is null, dropping team members' destination calendars instead of initializing the array

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which will no-op when `destinationCalendar` is `null`. Since `teamDestinationCalendars` can be populated from other team members even when the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar, this silently drops those calendars instead of initializing the array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] BaseCalendarService (CalendarManager.ts / CalendarService.ts) — `createEvent`/`listCalendars` also only use `destinationCalendar[0]` and ignore `credentialId`; per-credential loop will create events into the wrong calendar for non-Google providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and updates Google to select the calendar by `credentialId`, but `BaseCalendarService` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts) still derives behavior solely from the first element: it destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then filters/marks calendars using only `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (both in `createEvent`-path filtering and `listCalendars` primary flag). There is no selection by the `credentialId` passed from `CalendarManager.createEvent` (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`), so when `EventManager` loops per destination/credential, non-Google providers using this base logic can apply the wrong `externalId` (from destinationCalendar[0]) for a different credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts (google):145-149 — When credential's destination calendar isn't found, `createEvent` silently falls back to `"primary"`, booking the event on the wrong calendar instead of erroring

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` and then calls `calendar.events.insert` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If the event has `destinationCalendar` entries but none match the passed `credentialId`, this silently falls back to the user's primary calendar, which can create the event on the wrong calendar rather than failing or signaling a mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] EventManager.ts:~500-530 — In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, if the credential filter finds nothing and DB fetch fails or app slug is missing, `credential` remains `undefined` and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` throws a TypeError on a previously non-null path
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same underlying bug: in `updateAllCalendarEvents`, `credential` can remain `undefined` (e.g., when a credentialId is present but no matching credential is found), and then `updateEvent` is invoked with an undefined credential, causing a runtime/TypeError unless handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] EventManager.ts & handleCancelBooking.ts — `prisma.credential.findUnique` runs sequentially inside a per-reference/destination loop with duplicated logic; N destinations cause N sequential round-trips that could be batched

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new per-destination/per-reference loops that perform `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside a `for (const ...)` loop, which will execute sequentially and can cause N round-trips for N items. Examples: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and, when a credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, does an awaited `prisma.credential.findUnique` before continuing. Similarly, `EventManager.updateCalendarEvents` iterates `for (const reference of calendarReference)` and may await `prisma.credential.findUnique` per reference. `handleCancelBooking.ts` also loops calendar references and, when a user credential isn’t found, awaits `prisma.credential.findUnique` per reference. This is a diff-grounded performance/duplication concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] webhook.e2e.ts:249 — No test covers the new multi-destination collective flow (multiple destinationCalendar entries / multiple calendar references on update and delete), the core behavior change of the PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a core behavior change where `destinationCalendar` becomes an array and multi-destination collective flows are explicitly supported: e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calls `createEvent(..., destination.externalId)`, and update/delete paths now process *multiple* `_calendar` references via `.filter(...)` + loops (e.g., `updateCalendarEvent`, `handleCancelBooking`). The only shown e2e test change in `webhook.e2e.ts` is updating an expected payload field from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, which does not exercise multiple destination calendars or multiple calendar references on update/delete. So the finding about missing test coverage for the new multi-destination collective flow is specific and grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] CalendarManager.ts:229 — Typo fix changing "organiser" to "organizer" is a behavioral string change not covered by i18n TODO; tests/snapshots asserting the old string will break

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the literal string in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` from "Notes have been hidden by the organiser" to "...organizer" while the comment still says `// TODO: i18n this string?`, so it is a real user-facing copy change outside i18n. However, the claim that "tests/snapshots asserting the old string will break" is not verifiable from the provided diff (no related tests/snapshots shown), so it’s better treated as a non-bug review concern about unintended behavioral/copy change rather than a confirmed defect.
